findings.excerpt:
instance instFree (R A M : Type*)
    [CommSemiring R] [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M] [Module.Free R M]
    [CommSemiring A] [Algebra R A] :
    Module.Free A (A ⊗[R] M) :=
  Module.Free.of_basis <| Algebra.TensorProduct.basis A (Module.Free.chooseBasis R M)
findings.problem: The instance assumes `[CommSemiring A]`, but the construction immediately uses `Algebra.TensorProduct.basis`, whose surrounding section assumes only `[Semiring A] [Algebra R A]` (target lines 42 and 65), and `Module.Free.of_basis`, which also only needs a semiring. Thus the canonical base-change freeness instance is unnecessarily restricted to commutative algebras: for a noncommutative `R`-algebra `A`, the existing proof does not apply even though the basis construction and freeness proof do. This is a structural assumption that can be weakened, not an unused binder. The library already has the more general tensor-product freeness instance `Module.Free.tensor` under `[Semiring S]` (`Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/TensorProduct/Basis.lean`, line 196), which corroborates that semiring scalars are the natural setting.
findings.proposed_change:
Replace `[CommSemiring A]` by `[Semiring A]` in the instance signature:

```lean
instance instFree (R A M : Type*)
    [CommSemiring R] [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M] [Module.Free R M]
    [Semiring A] [Algebra R A] :
    Module.Free A (A ⊗[R] M) :=
  Module.Free.of_basis <| Algebra.TensorProduct.basis A (Module.Free.chooseBasis R M)
```

The proof body is unchanged; `Algebra.TensorProduct.basis` is available because the `Basis` section only requires `[Semiring A] [Algebra R A]`, and `Module.Free.of_basis` requires only `[Semiring A]` for the scalar type.
findings.benefit: Users obtain the freeness of `A ⊗[R] M` for noncommutative `R`-algebras such as matrix algebras over a commutative ring `R`, without having to find a separate tensor-product instance. The commutative case is merely a special case, so existing uses are not lost, and the instance becomes consistent with the file's own basis construction.
